description_i18n.id:
Dihtortion punya dua kepribadian, dipilih lewat toggle **AMP MODE**.

*Raw distortion* adalah taman bermain waveshaping: delapan kurva transfer yang melewati satu mesin anti-aliasing. *Amp Mode* adalah amplifier gitar penuh dengan jalur amp yang dimodelkan secara fisik, empat cabinet, dan impulse response ruangan.

Ditulis dalam C++17 di atas JUCE 7.0.12.

latest.changelog:
## What's New in 2.0.0

### Room IR Loader

A second convolution stage now sits **after** the cabinet, loaded with six
rooms captured in-house:

| Space | Character |
|---|---|
| **Small Room** | Tight, close ambience |
| **Garage** | Boxy, mid-forward slap |
| **Hallway** | Narrow with a long flutter |
| **Kitchen** | Hard surfaces, bright reflections |
| **Car Interior** | Very short, dense, heavily damped |
| **Auditorium** | Wide, long tail |

It opens as its own page from the **ROOM** link sitting between the CABINET and
OUTPUT panels, so the main view stays uncluttered and the bottom row now reads
as the actual signal path: `CABINET > ROOM > OUTPUT`.

**This stage is deliberately bare.** Convolution and a dry/wet blend, nothing
else. No EQ, no filtering, no tonal shaping, so each space sounds exactly as it
was recorded.

**Controls**

- **SPACE** picks the room, or **Off**, which costs no CPU at all.
- **DRY** and **WET** are independent level controls (-60 to +6 dB), so you can
  lift the room without thinning the direct sound.
- **DECAY** (5 to 100 %) shortens the tail. At 100 % the captured room is left
  completely untouched.

The dry path is delay-compensated against the convolver, so the two never
phase-cancel when summed. Long room impulses are handled by a non-uniform
partitioned engine, which keeps them affordable at zero added latency.

### Interface

- New **ROOM** chain link between CABINET and OUTPUT, drawn in the same style
  as the panels either side of it, with flow chevrons showing the routing.
- The X-Y transfer tracer stays visible on the room page, so you can still watch
  the signal while setting levels.
- Buttons now follow the plugin's own styling instead of the framework default.

# Dihtortion

**A VST3 guitar amplifier simulator and asymmetric wavefolder for Windows.**
**Eight shaper types, four cabinets, and a physically-modelled amp path, written in C++17 on JUCE.**

---

## Overview

Dihtortion has two personalities, switched by the **AMP MODE** toggle.

**Raw distortion** is a waveshaping playground: eight transfer curves running
through one anti-aliased engine. **Amp Mode** is a full guitar amplifier, with
cascaded gain stages, a four-band tone stack, cabinet convolution, a room IR
loader, and a lead channel voiced separately from rhythm.

Both modes share an **X-Y transfer curve tracer**, an oscilloscope in X-Y mode
plotting input against output, so you watch the actual transfer function move
while you play. The accent colour follows the active mode.

### Distortion Mode

![Distortion mode](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ClyntiaAikaHanaa/Dihtortion/HEAD/screenshot/DISTORTION%20MODE.png)

## Controls

### INPUT (both modes)

| Control | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| **PRE GAIN** | -12 to +30 dB | 0 dB | Level into the saturation chain. This is the main "how hard am I hitting it" control. Everything downstream is level-dependent, so it shapes feel as much as loudness. |
| **DRIVE** / **AMP GAIN** | 1 to 20 | 1.0 | Gain inside each saturation stage. The total is split across the cascade (each stage gets `√drive`), so raising it thickens harmonics rather than just getting louder. In Amp Mode it is capped at 15 and relabelled **AMP GAIN**. |

### SHAPER (raw distortion mode only)

| Control | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| **TYPE** | 8 curves | Fold | Selects the waveshaping function (see table below). |
| **FOLD** | 0 to 1 | 0.0 | The *character* knob. Its meaning follows TYPE, and the label changes with it: FOLD, BIAS, HYST, EDGE, GATE, RECT, CEIL, KNEE. |
| **ASYM** | -5 to +5 | 0.0 | Asymmetry. Pushes the curve off-centre to generate **even** harmonics, the "warm/octave" quality. In Fold it uses a Gaussian term; in every other type it is a bias offset, so the asymmetry survives at high drive instead of fading out. |
| **TONE** | 500 Hz to 20 kHz | 20 kHz | One-pole low-pass **before** the clipper. Filtering pre-distortion changes which harmonics get *generated*, which is very different from EQ'ing afterwards. |

#### Shaper types

| Type | Curve | Character | FOLD knob becomes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Fold** | Asymmetric wavefolder | The plugin's signature. Folds instead of clipping | Fold amount |
| **Tube** | `tanh` + grid bias | Warm, compressed, even harmonics | Bias depth |
| **Tape** | `atan` + hysteresis + HF self-erasure | Rounded, thick, darkens when driven | Hysteresis depth |
| **Diode** | Exponential clipper | Raspy, pedal-like, aggressive | Knee sharpness |
| **Fuzz** | Hard clip + dead zone | Velcro / gated fuzz | Gate width |
| **Octave** | Rectifier blend | Octave-up fuzz, ring-like on chords | Rectify amount |
| **Hard Clip** | Pure clamp | Precise, buzzy, honest digital edge | Ceiling |
| **Soft Clip** | Cubic to hard morph | Creamy, mild overdrive | Knee hardness |

### TONE STACK (Amp Mode)

Modelled on a real tone stack: these run **before** the power stages, so they
change what the distortion is fed, not just the final EQ.

| Control | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| **BASS** | 0 to 10 | 5.0 | Low shelf around 190 Hz. |
| **MID** | 0 to 10 | 5.0 | Drives two bands (461 Hz and 693 Hz) together. Lowering it produces the scooped voicing, raising it pushes the amp forward. |
| **PRES** | 0 to 10 | 8.0 | Upper-mid presence. **Above 5** it also engages a post-distortion high shelf at 3.9 kHz (up to +5 dB), because real presence controls are power-amp boosts. That half of the range adds air rather than only cutting. |
| **HIGH** | 0 to 10 | 7.0 | Below 5 it sweeps a 3.2 kHz shelf from -10 dB to flat. Above 5 it opens a four-band treble boost (up to +15 dB at 3.7 kHz). White-noise injection is compensated as this rises, so the hiss floor stays put. |

### CABINET (Amp Mode)

| Control | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| **MODEL** | 4 cabinets | US Modern | Impulse-response convolution. Each cabinet carries its own correction EQ. |
| **TONE** | 0 to 100 % | 73 % | Post-cab tilt filter: low-pass below the midpoint, high-pass above it. |

| Cabinet | Source |
|---|---|
| **US Modern** | Original in-house capture, calibrated and baked in |
| **US Vintage**, **British Classic**, **Boutique** | From BYOD (GPL-3.0) |

### ROOM (Amp Mode)

A second convolution stage sitting **after** the cabinet, loaded with six rooms
captured in-house. It opens as its own page from the **ROOM** link between the
CABINET and OUTPUT panels, so the main view stays uncluttered and the bottom
row reads as the actual signal chain: `CABINET > ROOM > OUTPUT`.

This stage is deliberately bare. Convolution and a dry/wet blend, nothing else:
no EQ, no filtering, no tonal shaping, so each space sounds exactly as recorded.

| Control | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPACE** | Off + 6 rooms | Off | Small Room, Garage, Hallway, Kitchen, Car Interior, Auditorium. Off costs no CPU at all. |
| **DRY** | -60 to +6 dB | 0 dB | Level of the unprocessed signal. Independent of WET, so you can lift the room without thinning the direct sound. |
| **WET** | -60 to +6 dB | -12 dB | Level of the convolved room. |
| **DECAY** | 5 to 100 % | 100 % | At 100 % the captured tail is left completely untouched. Below that, an exponential window reaching -60 dB at (decay x length) shortens the reverberation time. |

### OUTPUT (both modes)

| Control | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| **LEVEL** | -24 to +24 dB | 0 dB | Final output gain. Lead Amp automatically trims a further -3 dB to keep rhythm and lead balanced. |
| **OVERSAMPLE** | Off / 2x / 4x | 4x | Runs the nonlinear stages at a multiple of the sample rate. The engine already uses ADAA, so **2x is often indistinguishable from 4x** at roughly half the cost. Worth A/B testing. |

### Mode switches

| Switch | What it does |
|---|---|
| **AMP MODE** | Swaps the shaper section for the full amp: tone stack, cabinet, power-amp modelling, noise floor. Locks the engine to the Fold curve. |
| **LEAD AMP** | A separately voiced lead channel with tighter lows, a Tube-Screamer-style mid push, pre-distortion compression, and a third gain stage. Rhythm settings are untouched. |

---

## DSP structure

Signal flow in Amp Mode, in order:

```
INPUT
  |
  |- Silence bypass ......... skips the whole chain when idle
  |- Transient sidechain .... 3 kHz+ pick-click detector (feeds the low duck)
  |- Noise injection ........ 50 Hz hum + hiss, input-keyed gate
  |- Source high-cut ........ 12th-order Butterworth LPF @ 3.09 kHz
  |- Tone stack ............. 13 bands
  |- Pre-EQ ................. 17 bands
  |- Lead voicing ........... HPF 130 Hz > mid boost > compressor   [lead only]
  |
  === OVERSAMPLING (2x / 4x) ======================================
  |  |- Tone filter + Miller effect .... dynamic pre-clip low-pass
  |  |- Power-supply sag ............... bounded envelope
  |  |- PSU ripple ..................... 100 Hz drive modulation
  |  |- Dynamic crunch ................. AGC lift + bias + tighten
  |  |- Saturation stages 1 > 2 > 3 .... ADAA wavefolder cascade
  =================================================================
  |
  |- Presence boost ......... post-distortion shelf
  |- Transformer saturation . 120 Hz crossover, low band only
  |- Post-EQ ................ 10 bands
  |- Dynamic power section .. NFB collapse + speaker resonance
  |- Low-end group delay .... 6 all-pass sections
  |- Transient low duck ..... bass steps aside for the pick
  |- Cabinet convolution .... IR + tone filter + correction EQ
  |- Room convolution ....... pure IR + dry/wet, no EQ        [when SPACE is on]
  |- Output gain
OUTPUT
```

### Anti-derivative anti-aliasing (ADAA)

Every saturation stage is evaluated through the **antiderivative** of its
transfer function rather than the function itself:

```
y[n] = ( F(x[n]) - F(x[n-1]) ) / ( x[n] - x[n-1] )
```

This averages the curve across the sample interval instead of point-sampling
it, which suppresses the aliasing a hard nonlinearity would otherwise fold back
into the audible band. Each of the eight shaper types ships with a closed-form
antiderivative, so anti-aliasing quality is identical across all of them.

The `log(cosh(x))` term is evaluated in a numerically stable form,
`|x| + log1p(e^-2|x|) - ln 2`, because the naive version overflows `float` past
`|x| = 89` and produces NaN that latches every downstream filter into silence.

### Amp behaviour that a static curve cannot produce

| Model | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Power-supply sag** | Gain dips after a transient and recovers over roughly 150 ms. The detector reads a `tanh`-bounded copy of the signal, mirroring how real sag follows current on an already-compressed waveform, and keeping the effect bounded instead of pumping. |
| **Dynamic power section** | When the stages are pushed hard, the negative-feedback loop loses grip: speaker resonance (around 100 Hz) and presence (above 4.5 kHz) bloom, then settle as the note decays. |
| **Rectifier ripple** | 100 Hz supply ripple multiplies drive, creating true intermodulation sidebands at `f ± 100 Hz`, the "ghost notes" of vintage amps. Multiplicative, so it is silent when nothing plays. |
| **Low-end group delay** | Six all-pass sections delay the lows progressively (about 5 ms at 300 Hz, 18 ms at 70 Hz) with a perfectly flat magnitude response. Bass arrives *behind* the pick attack, the way a speaker's resonance rings up. |
| **Transient low duck** | Each pick attack briefly steps the sub-300 Hz band aside. A ring-ratio discriminator tells palm mutes from ringing chords, so chugs stay tight while open strums keep their body. |
| **Dynamic crunch** | Soft picking is lifted toward the player's own recent peak by a self-calibrating AGC, with tube bias and the crossover dead zone tracking the same envelope. Crunch is present at low velocity without a static boost, and the gain knob keeps its meaning. |
| **Thermal drift** | Two slow, mutually detuned LFOs continuously nudge input voltage and tube bias, so the amp never sounds perfectly static. |

### Performance

- Filter coefficients are rebuilt only when a control actually moves, so there
  is no filter design or heap allocation on the audio thread.
- Impulse responses are decoded once at startup, never on the audio thread.
- Idle input short-circuits the whole chain after a guard interval.
- Per-sample constants are hoisted out of the ADAA inner loop.

## Building

Requires **CMake 3.22+** and a C++17 compiler. JUCE is fetched automatically.

```bash
cmake -B build -S .
cmake --build build --config Release
```

The VST3 is copied to the system plug-in folder after a successful build.

### Windows installer

With Inno Setup 6:

```powershell
powershell -File Installer/make_assets.ps1
& "C:\Program Files (x86)\Inno Setup 6\ISCC.exe" Installer\Dihtortion.iss
```

Output lands in `Installer/Output/`.

## ⚠️ Listening safety

This is a high-gain processor. Pre Gain, Drive and the tone stack can raise the
output level a great deal, and high-gain settings produce dense, sustained
signals far louder than the input.

**Keep monitoring low while adjusting, and put a limiter on your master.**
Protect your hearing, it does not grow back.
